rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 scored 462.9, the best so far. It finished all 20 oval runs (progress 0.998) but left the track on 18 of 20 s-bend runs and all 20 slalom runs. Each run averaged about 1.05 to 1.1 line-loss events, and steering_oscillation was high on the bends (0.23 slalom, 0.39 s-bend). Moving the sensor row forward from y=0.03 to y=0.05 was the largest gain, so the controller benefits from seeing the line earlier. The outer sensors at x=±0.036 with 12 mm footprints lose the tape once its edge passes about 0.055 m off-centre, which is close to the 0.06 m off-track limit. That leaves little margin for the error to recover after a line loss.

Changes: (1) Move the sensor row further forward to y=0.065 for more lead time on bends. (2) Widen the array to x=±0.042 with 14 mm spacing, so the line stays visible up to about 6 cm of offset. Weights stay linear at -2 to +2, so the outer weight-to-position ratio drops about 14 percent, which also reduces the gain that caused the high oscillation on the s-bend. (3) Raise kd from 0.4 to 0.5 to damp the jitter, since sensing now starts earlier and the loop is more lag-prone. (4) Keep kp 3.0, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, mass 0.5, wheel_track 0.12 and body 0.15 x 0.12 m, so the oval result is preserved.

Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom, steering_oscillation below 0.25, and s-bend and slalom progress above 0.6. The oval should still finish. Hypotheses: (a) the wider array and forward sensors cut line loss on bends; (b) the modest gain reduction plus kd 0.5 lowers the oscillation seen on the s-bend. Failure signs: progress stuck near 0.3 on the slalom with few line losses means kp is too low or speed too high; oscillation above 0.3 means kd or kp is still too high. Next measurements: line_loss_events and progress on s-bend and slalom show whether the forward, wider array holds the tape; steering_oscillation and max_error show whether the gains are balanced; completion_time shows the speed margin.
